The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — burned out, ready to give up — and how God met him with gentleness, rest, and provision before calling him onward.

The Parable of the Prodigal Son — a young man demands his inheritance, wastes it all, and returns home in shame, only to be met by a father who runs to embrace him before he can even finish his apology.

The story of Joseph — sold into slavery by his own brothers, falsely imprisoned, and seemingly forgotten — yet through every betrayal and setback, God was quietly at work, ultimately raising Joseph to a position where he could save countless lives, including the very brothers who had wronged him.

The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a man of unwavering faith who refused to stop praying even under threat of death, and whom God protected through the night, turning a trap set by his enemies into a testimony that echoed across a kingdom.
The story of Ruth and Naomi — loyalty, loss, and unexpected redemption as a young widow refuses to abandon her mother-in-law and finds belonging, purpose, and grace in a foreign land.
The story of David and Goliath — a young shepherd boy steps forward to face a giant warrior that an entire army feared, armed with nothing but a sling, five stones, and an unshakeable trust in God.

The Parable of the Good Samaritan — a man left for dead on a dangerous road is ignored by the very people expected to help, but is shown extraordinary compassion by an unlikely stranger, redefining what it truly means to love your neighbor.

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a king's golden idol and were thrown into a furnace so hot it killed the soldiers who cast them in, yet walked out unharmed, with a mysterious fourth figure seen walking beside them in the flames.

The story of Esther — a young Jewish woman who becomes queen of Persia and risks her life to approach the king unbidden, saving her entire people from a plot to destroy them, and discovering that perhaps she was placed exactly where she was "for such a time as this."

The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran from God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and after a second chance, delivered a message to Nineveh that sparked one of the most remarkable turnarounds in Scripture.
The story of the Feeding of the Five Thousand — a massive crowd, a boy's small lunch, and how Jesus took what little was offered and multiplied it into more than enough for everyone.

The story of Noah's Ark — God calls an ordinary man to an extraordinary task, Noah trusts and obeys through years of uncertainty, and a devastating flood gives way to a rainbow and a covenant of grace.

The story of the Paralyzed Man Lowered Through the Roof — four friends who refused to let any obstacle stop them from bringing someone they loved to Jesus, and the healing that followed their extraordinary act of faith.

The story of the Burning Bush — how God met Moses in the wilderness in an ordinary moment that became a turning point, calling a reluctant, self-doubting shepherd into one of the greatest missions in Scripture.

The story of the Walking on Water — Jesus comes to his frightened disciples across a stormy sea in the middle of the night, and Peter steps out of the boat in faith, only to begin sinking the moment his eyes leave Jesus.
The story of Mary and Martha — two sisters who welcome Jesus into their home, and what unfolds reveals a timeless truth about what it means to truly sit in God's presence.

The story of the woman at the well — a Samaritan woman with a complicated past meets Jesus alone at a well in the middle of the day, and a simple conversation about water becomes one of the most profound moments of grace and recognition in all of Scripture.

The story of the Transfiguration — Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, where his appearance is transformed in dazzling light, Moses and Elijah appear beside him, and the disciples hear the voice of God, leaving them overwhelmed and forever changed.
The story of the Widow's Offering — a poor woman quietly drops two small coins into the temple treasury, and Jesus tells his disciples that she has given more than all the wealthy donors combined.

The story of Zacchaeus — a despised tax collector who climbs a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus, and finds himself not only seen but personally invited into a life-changing encounter that transforms him completely.
The story of Abraham and Isaac on Mount Moriah — a father asked to give up what he loves most, who trusts God completely, and discovers that God himself provides at the very moment of surrender.
The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — a burnt-out prophet who wanted to give up, and the tender, unexpected way God met him in his exhaustion.

The Parable of the Prodigal Son — a young man demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, and hits rock bottom, yet when he finally turns back toward home, his father is already running to meet him with open arms.
The story of Joseph — sold into slavery by his own brothers, falsely imprisoned, and forgotten, yet rising to save nations and ultimately forgiving the very people who betrayed him.
